pictures.scene: Juan de Juanes, The Last Supper — Christ seated at the middle of a long white draped table in a grey violet robe with a crimson mantle, holding up a round white host in one lifted hand and laying the other on His breast, Peter with his name written in gold on his halo turning to Him grey bearded and open mouthed at the left, John in green leaning in at His shoulder with his hands spread wide, more apostles pointing in at both edges, and on the cloth in front of them a broad silver dish, a gold footed chalice, loaves of bread, knives and a little salt cellar, with bare feet under the table on a chequered marble floor and a green landscape seen through the arch behind, having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the very end, …
pictures.name: pd_juanes_last_supper

pictures.scene: Diego Velazquez, The Waterseller of Seville — a weathered old water carrier standing in a worn brown cloak split at the shoulder and the elbow over a white shirt, his lined face bent in profile, one hand laid on the neck of a great pale clay jar that stands beaded with water in front of him and the other holding out a tall glass of clear water, a boy in a dark coat with a white collar reaching in to take the glass with both hands, a second huge jar at the left edge, and a dim third face drinking in the shadow behind them, with nothing but plain dark brown above, so he got up from the supper, laid aside his outer garments, and wrapped a towel around his waist, …
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_waterseller

pictures.scene: Garofalo, Christ Washing the Disciples' Feet — Christ kneeling low on the pale stone floor in a crimson robe with a white towel knotted round His waist and a finely rayed gold halo behind His head, holding Peter's bare foot in both hands over a shallow gold basin while the water runs off it in bright threads, Peter sitting above Him in a blue tunic and a great orange yellow mantle with one hand pressed to his chest and his white bearded face bent down in protest, and behind them a close press of haloed apostles in green, red and gold leaning in to watch, against a worked grey stone wall and panelling, he came to simon peter, who asked him, lord, are you going to wash my feet, …
pictures.name: pd_garofalo_christ_washing_the_disciples_feet

pictures.scene: El Greco, The Tears of Saint Peter — an old apostle standing alone in the dark with his eyes brimming and lifted away to one side, his white hair and broad white beard catching the light, a great golden yellow mantle wrapped across him over a deep blue green robe open at the throat, his two big weathered hands clasped together in front of him with the heavy iron keys hanging from a cord at his wrist, trails of green ivy coming down out of the dark rock above him on both sides and a faint pale glimmer of sky far off at the left, never shall you wash my feet, peter told him, unless i wash you, you have no part with me, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_saint_peter_in_tears

pictures.scene: King David Kneeling before the Altar — a red bearded king down on both knees in burnished steel armour over a scarlet robe, a jewelled gold crown set on his head, a great stiff gold cope spread round him worked with little painted scenes in its medallions, one bare foot showing under the hem, his face turned up with his mouth open and his hand laid flat on his chest, a tall gilded harp leaning in against his knee, a white robed angel sweeping down out of the cloud at the upper left with one broad wing raised, a looped red curtain with a tasselled cord above him, and at the right edge two hands holding an open book lettered in Latin, then, lord, simon peter replied, not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well, …
pictures.name: pd_king_david_kneeling_before_an_altar

pictures.scene: Heinrich Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — Christ standing close in a rust red robe under a dark blue green mantle, His long hair falling at His shoulders and His eyes held steadily on the young man beside Him, one hand opened out and reaching away past the edge of the picture as He speaks, and the rich young man turned in against Him in a cream silk mantle over a sea green sleeved robe with a sash and an embroidered band, a jewelled clasp in his turban, his handsome face lowered and his hands folded in front of him, against a plain dim stone wall with a faint warm glow behind their heads, for he knew who would betray him, do you know what i have done for you, …
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Saint Peter Preaching — a fresco in soft chalky colour, the old apostle standing barefoot on a low step at the left in a pale blue tunic under a deep orange mantle with a gold halo behind his white head, one hand raised with two fingers up as he speaks and his face turned down toward the people, and gathered close in front of him a crowd of listeners, women in blue and rose veils kneeling with their hands hidden in their robes, an old white bearded man seated with his head bowed, ranks of caps, hoods and upturned faces behind, and white robed brothers crowding in at the right edge, under a green wooded mountain and a pale cliff, you call me teacher and lord, and rightly so, because i am, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_saint_peter_preaching

pictures.scene: Konrad Witz, Saint Christopher — a big bearded man wading waist deep across a green river in a heavy scarlet cloak, bent far over under his load with his face strained and lowered, gripping a rough forked staff driven into the water with one raised hand and holding the other out for balance, and riding high on his shoulder a small fair haired child in a plain grey robe with a little gold crown of rays, one hand lifted in blessing and the other holding on by the man's hair, with pale rock cliffs standing up at the right, low wooded banks, a far blue headland and two little rowing boats out on the still water behind, no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him, …
pictures.name: pd_witz_christoffel

pictures.scene: Juan Sanchez Cotan, Quince, Cabbage and Melon — a bare grey stone window ledge running across the bottom of a deep velvety black opening, with a yellow quince hung on a fine cord at the upper left, its two green leaves still on the stalk, a great ruffled green cabbage hung on a second cord below it with its outer leaves curling open and one leaf drooping low, and set down on the stone at the right a pale netted melon with a wedge cut out of it showing the soft rose flesh and the wet seeds in the hollow, every one of them lit from the left and glowing against the dark, the one who shares my bread has lifted up his heel against me, …
pictures.name: pd_cotan_brood

pictures.scene: Hans Memling, Christ Giving His Blessing — one enormous half length Christ facing straight out of the panel, His long brown hair falling in soft waves on both shoulders, a short forked beard, and wide calm grey eyes looking directly at the viewer, a deep crimson robe over His shoulders, one hand lifted in front of His breast with two fingers raised in blessing and the thumb drawn in, the fingers of a second pair of hands just showing at the lower edge, and behind His head a great burnished gold halo scored all round with fine ruled rays, bordered by dark blue grey clouds in the corners of the panel, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that i am he, …
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_blessing

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Supper at Emmaus — a small round table covered with a brilliant white cloth standing in a dim vaulted stone hall, Christ seated behind it in a pale rose robe with a grey brown mantle fallen over His arm, a faint rayed glory breaking out of the dark behind His head, His tired face lifted and His two hands just breaking a round loaf over a pewter plate, one companion seated at the left with his back half turned and his hand raised to his mouth as he stares across at Him, an old grey bearded man at the right gripping the table edge and leaning in open mouthed, a young serving man standing between them holding out a dish of meat, pewter plates, a glass and a napkin set out on the cloth, and worked brown stone, a great dark arch and a far pier rising behind, he became troubled in spirit and testified, truly, truly, i tell you, one of you will betray me, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_supper_at_emmaus

lines.text: It was now just before the Passover Feast, and Jesus knew that His hour had come to leave this world and return to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the very end.
The evening meal was underway, and the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus.
Jesus knew that the Father had delivered all things into His hands, and that He had come from God and was returning to God.
So He got up from the supper, laid aside His outer garments, and wrapped a towel around His waist.
After that, He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet and dry them with the towel that was around Him.
He came to Simon Peter, who asked Him, Lord, are You going to wash my feet?
Jesus replied, You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.
Never shall You wash my feet! Peter told Him. Jesus answered, Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me.
Then, Lord, Simon Peter replied, not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!
Jesus told him, Whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean. And you are clean, though not all of you.
For He knew who would betray Him. That is why He said, Not all of you are clean.
When Jesus had washed their feet and put on His outer garments, He reclined with them again and asked, Do you know what I have done for you?
You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another's feet.
I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.
Truly, truly, I tell you, no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them.
I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is to fulfill the Scripture: The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.
I am telling you now before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that I am He.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives the one I send receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.
After Jesus had said this, He became troubled in spirit and testified, Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray Me.
The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant.
One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side.
So Simon Peter motioned to him to ask Jesus which one He was talking about.
Leaning back against Jesus, he asked, Lord, who is it?
Jesus answered, It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it. Then He dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
And when Judas had taken the morsel, Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to Judas, What you are about to do, do quickly.
But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him.
Since Judas kept the money bag, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night.
When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him.
If God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify the Son in Himself, and will glorify Him at once.
Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for Me, and as I said to the Jews, so now I say to you: Where I am going, you cannot come.
A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.
Lord, where are You going? Simon Peter asked. Jesus answered, Where I am going, you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow later.
Lord, said Peter, why can't I follow You now? I will lay down my life for You.
Will you lay down your life for Me? Jesus replied. Truly, truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.
